events.title: Hubble gets corrective optics
events.description: Astronauts service the space telescope to improve its images.

events.title: South Africa holds a democratic election
events.description: The country holds its first national democratic election open to all races.

events.title: Windows 95 reaches stores
events.description: Microsoft launches a new operating system with a Start menu and taskbar.

what_happened_next.text:
IBM more than tripled, leading these choices after a difficult early stretch. Ford, Disney and the US basket also more than doubled. A famous company could struggle and recover, but a recovery was never guaranteed. This result should not turn every troubled company into an automatic bargain.

During the period, astronauts repaired Hubble, South Africa held its first national democratic election open to all races, and Windows 95 reached shops. Changes in science, politics and everyday technology continued while people held their investments. These events explain the setting, but they do not pin each rise or fall in a share price to one cause.

Look at IBM’s difficult months before its recovery. Would you have stayed with your original choice? The game lets you see the whole route at once; an investor then received only the next piece of news. A low price can reflect a genuine problem as well as a possible opportunity, so a later recovery should not be treated as inevitable.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Clinton was preparing to take office, carmakers had mixed fortunes, and researchers were testing cleaner ways to wash clothes.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Company paths mattered over the entire holding period. Ending well did not mean avoiding losses along the way, and these three shares did not represent every business.
reflection.what_faded_away: The excitement of a new presidency and a holiday movie did not reveal the final stock ranking. Interesting news and useful price forecasts are different things.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: IBM’s eventual lead could not be read from its starting reputation or partnerships. Investors still had to face uncertainty while events unfolded.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: Ford sold a record 2.1 million trucks in the United States in 1996 and launched the Expedition SUV that October. Total annual profit reached about $4.4 billion. Europe’s car business still lost money, so the improvement was uneven. Strong truck demand was a concrete business success during Ford’s large five-year investment gain.

The Lion King became a major hit in 1994, and Disney completed its purchase of ABC in February 1996. That deal brought television networks and stations into the business alongside films and parks. The five-year investment rose strongly as Disney added successful entertainment and a much larger television business.

IBM was still in crisis when this round began. It returned to an annual profit of about $3 billion in 1994, bought Lotus in 1995 and expanded computer services. Services revenue reached about $12.7 billion in 1995. The large investment gain covered a recovery in earnings and a broader business beyond computer hardware.
